```{r}
#| context: setup
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(DT)

df <- diamonds
```

# Overview

## {.sidebar}

```{r}
selectInput("cut", "Diamond Cut",
            choices = c("All", levels(df$cut)))

sliderInput("carat", "Carat Range",
            min = 0, max = 5,
            value = c(0, 5), step = 0.1)

checkboxGroupInput("color", "Diamond Color",
                   choices = levels(df$color),
                   selected = levels(df$color))

radioButtons("clarity", "Clarity",
             choices = c("All", levels(df$clarity)))

numericInput("price", "Maximum Price",
             value = 20000, min = 0)
```

```{r}
#| context: server

filtered <- reactive({
  data <- df |>
    filter(carat >= input$carat[1],
           carat <= input$carat[2],
           color %in% input$color,
           price <= input$price)

  if (input$cut != "All") {
    data <- data |> filter(cut == input$cut)
  }

  if (input$clarity != "All") {
    data <- data |> filter(clarity == input$clarity)
  }

  data
})
```

## Row {height=20%}

```{r}
renderValueBox({
  value_box(
    title = "Total Diamonds",
    value = nrow(filtered()),
    showcase = icon("gem")
  )
})
```

```{r}
renderValueBox({
  value_box(
    title = "Average Price",
    value = paste0("$", round(mean(filtered()$price), 2)),
    showcase = icon("dollar-sign")
  )
})
```

## Row

### Price Distribution

```{r}
renderPlotly({
  p <- ggplot(filtered(), aes(x = price)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "Price ($)", y = "Number of Diamonds")

  ggplotly(p)
})
```

### Carat vs. Price

```{r}
renderPlotly({
  p <- ggplot(filtered(), aes(x = carat, y = price)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "steelblue") +
    theme_minimal()

  ggplotly(p)
})
```

# Analysis

## Column {.tabset}

### Price by Cut

```{r}
ggplotly(
  ggplot(df, aes(x = cut, y = price, fill = cut)) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "Cut", y = "Price ($)")
)
```

### Average Price by Color

```{r}
df |>
  group_by(color) |>
  summarize(avg_price = mean(price)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = color, y = avg_price, fill = color)) +
  geom_col() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Color", y = "Average Price ($)")
```

### Average Price by Clarity

```{r}
df |>
  group_by(clarity) |>
  summarize(avg_price = mean(price)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = clarity, y = avg_price, fill = clarity)) +
  geom_col() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Clarity", y = "Average Price ($)")
```

### Findings

The dashboard shows that diamond prices generally increase
as carat weight increases. Price also varies across cut,
color and clarity categories. However, differences in average
prices do not necessarily mean that one quality category
causes higher prices, because carat weight also influences
the results.
